title: Use the Final Five Minutes
prompt: We are at the final part of a fictional interview for a role on a small service team. Ask questions that help you understand whether the role fits your goals. I will answer as the hiring manager. Ask one question at a time and follow up on useful details. You can ask about expectations, working conditions, learning, support, or anything else relevant to your decision.
blurb: Practice questions about expectations, support, working conditions, and real examples so you can judge role fit.

rubric.label: Relevant inquiry
rubric.description: Connects questions to the role, personal priorities and information still missing.

anchors.0: Asks only questions unrelated to the role despite clarification.
anchors.2: Asks about an actual role responsibility or a personal work priority.
anchors.4: Connects a priority to a specific responsibility and asks what would make the role a fit.

rubric.label: Active follow-up
rubric.description: Uses the interviewer’s answer to deepen the next question.

anchors.0: Repeatedly ignores answers and restarts the same question.
anchors.2: Uses a supplied answer to ask one relevant follow-up.
anchors.4: Follows an answer to resolve a material uncertainty without repeating what was already answered.

rubric.label: Concrete evidence
rubric.description: Asks for examples instead of accepting broad culture claims.

anchors.0: Treats broad unsupported claims as verified examples.
anchors.2: Asks for a concrete example of a team practice or challenge.
anchors.4: Uses a concrete example to distinguish a stated aspiration from actual practice.

rubric.label: Decision usefulness
rubric.description: Investigates expectations, support and tradeoffs relevant to a fit decision.

anchors.0: Makes a fit judgment based on facts the interviewer explicitly says are unknown.
anchors.2: Explores one condition or expectation that could affect fit.
anchors.4: Compares a tradeoff relevant to their own priorities and identifies information still needed.

rubric.label: Prioritization
rubric.description: Uses limited time for important questions rather than exhausting a memorized list.

anchors.0: Continues unrelated questions without allowing answers or responding to time cues.
anchors.2: Prioritizes one or two relevant questions and listens to the answers.
anchors.4: Uses the available time to resolve the most decision-relevant uncertainty and leaves lower priorities for follow-up.

rubric.label: Fit reflection
rubric.description: Summarizes what was learned and what remains uncertain without overclaiming.

anchors.0: Claims a guarantee of role fit or working conditions not provided.
anchors.2: Summarizes a known fact and one remaining uncertainty.
anchors.4: Explains how a specific answer informs their decision and what additional evidence would change it.

reference.scenario: We are at the final part of a fictional interview for a role on a small service team. Ask questions that help you understand whether the role fits your goals. I will answer as the hiring manager. Ask one question at a time and follow up on useful details. You can ask about expectations, working conditions, learning, support, or anything else relevant to your decision.

facts.value: The first three months focus on improving one recurring service task with a mentor.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about success or initial expectations

facts.value: The team documents major decisions asynchronously and has two shared meeting blocks per week.
A recent service improvement slipped because ownership between two teams was unclear. The team is trialing a single-owner decision log.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks for a challenge or concrete example

facts.value: A mentor meets weekly; urgent questions go to a rotating support partner.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about support or onboarding

model_points: Connects questions to the role, personal priorities and information still missing.
Uses the interviewer’s answer to deepen the next question.
Asks for examples instead of accepting broad culture claims.
Investigates expectations, support and tradeoffs relevant to a fit decision.
Uses limited time for important questions rather than exhausting a memorized list.
Summarizes what was learned and what remains uncertain without overclaiming.

probes.question: Is there a specific example you would like me to explain?
What did you learn that would matter to your decision?

follow_ups: What additional evidence would change your decision?
reference.exemplar_answer: Multiple approaches are valid. A strong response establishes the goal, uses the provided facts, tests alternatives, explains tradeoffs, and states uncertainty.

interviewer_notes: Roleplay only this fictional team. Do not invent compensation, legal policies, company names or personal history. Say when a fact is unspecified. Do not score candidates down for reasonable questions about working conditions or support. Do not assume a technology role or score personal priorities as good or bad. Asking about support, working conditions, compensation, or accessibility is legitimate; unspecified terms stay unknown.

learning_drills.title: Repair one decision
learning_drills.prompt: Choose one decision in your answer. Rewrite the explanation using one fact, one alternative, and one limitation. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: State what would change your mind
